requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The only source change is in TypeCollector.cs, in two member loops: one that, judging by the code shape, handles properties, and one that handles fields. In each loop it adds a `continue` after the 'mixed string and int keys' diagnostic. It also guards the int-key and string-key dictionary `Add` calls so a duplicate key no longer throws. Before this, a mixed-key member hit `intKey!.Value` on a null key, and a duplicate key made `Dictionary.Add` throw. Either exception would crash the analyzer and lose its diagnostics. The change also adds analyzer tests that check suppressed types are still validated, two execution tests, and a README section.
story.why: The issue says the analyzer stopped reporting for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types from 3.1.1. The author's apparent theory is that an exception inside TypeCollector kills the analyzer. The diff never touches any `SuppressSourceGeneration` handling. If the 3.1.1 regression was instead that suppressed types are skipped, the root cause is not addressed here. In that case the new MsgPack004/003/015 tests show whether it already works, not that this change fixed it.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains an 'Opting out of source generation' section that documents which analyzer rules do and do not apply to suppressed types.
New execution tests check that no formatter is generated and that a round-trip works through the dynamic resolver. This is runtime and generator behaviour, not the analyzer.
The duplicate-key and mixed-key guards also change behaviour for normal (non-suppressed) types, which also go through TypeCollector.

findings.description: Claim C14 disputed: Over-citation on README.md lines 1622-1623: C14 cites lines 1620-1633 while only describing the analyzer-rule bullets on lines 1625-1632, omitting the runtime resolver and AOT-safety claims on lines 1622-1623 ('No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which fall back to a precompiled formatter when one is available, so such a type remains AOT-safe.'). Moreover, that unmentioned statement on line 1623 is inaccurate when no custom formatter exists because dynamic resolvers require runtime code generation, which fails on AOT targets (see lines 1617-1618).

The diff never touches SuppressSourceGeneration handling; it only removes two crash paths. If the 3.1.1 regression is that suppressed types are skipped by the analyzer, the bug is not fixed here. The new MsgPack004/003/015 tests would then either already pass or fail; confirm they fail on the base commit.
The field-loop copies of the fix (continue and both duplicate-key guards) have no test. Every new test uses properties, which go through the other loop.

Duplicate-key members are now dropped silently from the member map. For non-suppressed types this relies on the MsgPack005 error stopping generation. If generation proceeds, the emitted formatter would omit the second member without any further signal.

The `continue` skips all later per-member processing, such as formatter-attribute and member-type checks. Other diagnostics, for example MsgPack003, are therefore no longer reported for a member that has a mismatched key kind.

README.md line 1623 states that for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)], 'No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which fall back to a precompiled formatter when one is available, so such a type remains AOT-safe.' Because source generation produces no precompiled formatter for the type (confirmed by SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.cs:23) and dynamic resolvers rely on runtime Reflection.Emit code generation (which does not work on AOT platforms such as IL2CPP/NativeAOT, as noted right above at README.md:1617-1618), a suppressed type without a manually supplied formatter is NOT AOT-safe and will fail at run time in AOT environments (while AOT analyzer warnings MsgPack016/017 are also suppressed per line 1632).
